method_note: FAST MODE, one round. Greece facts reused from the Greece pack (not re-fetched today). Italy US-side facts were NOT reused because they apply to US citizens; Australian equivalents were read fresh from the Italian Consulate in Adelaide. France, Indonesia (Bali) and Fiji read with Apify web-fetch.

facts.claim: Greece (gov.gr registry, foreign residents): the marriage licence is valid for 6 months.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Greece (gov.gr 'Issue of a civil marriage licence'): deadline of completion 8 days (one-week objection wait plus 1 day to grant); validity duration 6 months; if the marriage does not take place within six months of the newspaper notice, the notice must be repeated.
facts.publisher: Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services (mitos.gov.gr)
facts.use_note: This entry is for residents. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Athens: the licence is issued seven days after submission and verification of documents and is valid for six months. Every document lodged must have been issued within the last six months; a home-country marital status certificate within the last three months.
facts.use_note: Athens page serves residents. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Greece, abroad route: under Interior Ministry circular 1969/S.477 (4 Jan 2019), a foreign document certifying no impediment that also names the other future spouse is equivalent to a Greek marriage licence, so no Greek licence is issued. Chania asks non-residents for their own country's licence, translated and certified, showing its validity period and naming the person they will marry.
facts.use_note: Medium: circular decoded by hand from a legacy font. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Italy, US citizens only: non-EU public documents are valid six months from issue; the Italian Consulate in San Francisco says the Atto Notorio is valid 90 days.
facts.publisher: US Embassy and Consulates in Italy
facts.use_note: DO NOT USE for Australians. Recorded only to show it was checked. The Australian route is different (F-105 to F-107): the Italian Consulate in Adelaide gives the Atto Notorio 6 months, not 90 days.

facts.claim: Australian citizens marrying in Italy need a Nulla Osta, granted by the Australian Embassy in Rome under article 116 of the Italian Civil Code and presented to the Italian town council (comune) before the wedding. To get it, they first obtain an Atto Notorio, signed by the Australian citizen and four witnesses not related to the couple, either at the Italian consulate for their state of residence in Australia or at any tribunal in Italy.
facts.publisher: Consulate of Italy in Adelaide (Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
facts.use_note: Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Italian Consulate in Adelaide: 'The Atto Notorio has a validity of 6 months, so it cannot be requested before 6 months from the date of the wedding.'
facts.publisher: Consulate of Italy in Adelaide (Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
facts.use_note: Key validity fact for Australians. Medium only because it is one consulate's 2022 guide; Sydney and Melbourne consulates were not checked this round (see needs). Contrasts with the 90 days quoted for the US route (F-104). Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Italian Consulate in Adelaide: Australians marrying in Italy also need an original birth certificate and a Single Status Certificate from the state Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, each with an official Italian translation and both bearing a DFAT Apostille.
facts.publisher: Consulate of Italy in Adelaide (Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
facts.use_note: No official source read this round gives a 'issued within X months' rule for these Australian certificates in Italy. Do not state one.

facts.claim: France: 'Under French Law THE CERTIFICATE (which is produced in FRENCH by the Australian Embassy in Paris) is valid for only 90 days after the date of issue.' The certificate is the Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (certificat de coutume ou de non-opposition au mariage).
facts.use_note: Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: France: a marriage must take place at a Town Hall (mairie) to be legally recognised, and at least one of the applicants must be a French citizen or a legal resident of France. The Embassy tells couples to contact the mairie directly for its requirements.
facts.use_note: Important for the article: two Australians who do not live in France cannot simply fly in for a legal French wedding. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: France: the Australian Embassy says to check with local authorities whether the birth certificate has to be less than six months old. Processing of the CNI can take up to ten working days. A CNI already issued in English by a DFAT office in Australia must be translated by a sworn translator.
facts.use_note: The six-month birth certificate rule is phrased as 'check with local authorities', so write 'many mairies ask for a birth certificate issued within the last six months; confirm with yours', not as a national rule.

facts.claim: Indonesia (including Bali): an Australian marrying in Indonesia applies for a Certificate of No Impediment (CNI) from the Australian Embassy in Jakarta or a Consulate-General; Bali, NTB and NTT fall under the Australian Consulate-General in Bali. The local Civil Registry Office or KUA normally requires the CNI from the mission with jurisdiction.
facts.use_note: Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Indonesia: 'We do not place an expiry date on the CNI, however the local Civil Registry Office do not normally accept CNIs that were issued more than 3 months prior.'
facts.use_note: Key validity fact for Bali: no printed expiry, but plan on a CNI issued within 3 months of the wedding. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Indonesia: for non-Muslim marriages, couples lodge a Notice of Intention to Marry with the Civil Registry Office at least 10 days before the wedding, and the marriage must be registered there afterwards to be legal. Both parties must hold the same religion recognised by the Indonesian Government (Law No. 1 of 1974). A CNI is usually issued while you wait if documents are complete.
facts.use_note: The Embassy calls this 'a general guide only' and notes requirements vary by province. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Fiji: foreign visitors in the country for a short time may be granted a Special Licence to Marry, which waives the 21-day notice. The standard route is a Notice of Intention to Marry displayed for 21 consecutive days at a BDM registry. Foreigners need passports, a Certificate of Single Status, Certificate of Search or Certificate of No Legal Impediment, divorce or death papers if relevant, and two witnesses with photo ID.
facts.use_note: This official page gives no validity period for the special licence. Wedded Advisor confirms the current process.

facts.claim: Fiji Embassy in Japan: the special licence is 'valid only for 28 days from the date of issue', within which the marriage may be performed. The same page, further down, says it 'is valid for 21 days from the date of issue' and is effective within one working day of application.
facts.publisher: Embassy of the Republic of Fiji in Japan
facts.use_note: CONFLICT within one official page (28 vs 21 days), and the page looks old. Do not print a number. Safe line: 'Fiji's special licence is valid for only a few weeks from issue, so apply after you arrive and close to the date; your Wedded Advisor confirms the current period.' See needs.

facts.claim: Fiji: after the wedding, one original marriage certificate is given to the couple and the other is sent with the licence to the Registrar General's Office in Suva within 7 days. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is the designated authority for apostilles on Fijian public documents.

needs.detail: The 6-month Atto Notorio validity (F-106) comes from the Italian Consulate in Adelaide's 2022 guide. Sydney and Melbourne pages were not read this round. Also not confirmed: how long the Australian Embassy Rome's Nulla Osta is valid and how recent the BDM birth and single status certificates must be.

The Fiji Embassy in Japan page states both 28 days and 21 days (F-131). The Fiji Ministry of Foreign Affairs page gives no period. Confirm with the Registrar General's Office in Suva or a Fiji resort wedding team before printing a number.

F-111 says at least one party must be a French citizen or legal resident. Decide whether France stays in the article as a 'legal wedding' destination or is framed as a symbolic ceremony with legal paperwork at home.
The 3-month CNI acceptance (F-121) is described as normal practice of Civil Registry Offices, not law. Confirm current Denpasar and Badung practice.
Not read this round (no time). It may say whether the DFAT CNI names the intended spouse, which matters for the Greece abroad route (F-103).
